---
description: Author intake-scoped atomic requirements.
agent: agent
---

Require one explicit GitHub Requirement issue reference in the invocation,
either an issue number such as `#6` or the issue URL. If it is missing, stop
immediately and ask the Business Analyst to provide the Requirement issue
number. Do not search for, list, infer, or select an issue from repository
state, conversation history, recent activity, or open issues.

Verify that the supplied issue exists, has the `requirement` label, identifies
exactly one accepted `INTK-####`, and is activated at `Ready / Ready for
Drafting`. If any condition fails, stop and tell the Business Analyst what must
be corrected.

Select exactly one mode.

## Prepare mode

Use this mode when `--submit` is absent. Read the accepted intake, all converted
evidence linked by the issue, and repository context. Invoke
`intake-traceability` and `atomic-requirement-authoring`. First propose
evidence-grounded business capability/process groups for human review, then
author `specs/intakes/INTK-####/requirement-groups.yml` with stable
`INTK-####-GRP-##` IDs, contiguous display order, descriptions, and direct
evidence references. Empty groups are invalid. Extract atomic needs within the
reviewed groups and write authoritative
`specs/intakes/INTK-####/requirements/INTK-####-REQ-###.md` files, regenerate
the intake requirements index as `Intake -> Requirement Group -> Atomic REQs`,
run `python scripts/validate_reqs.py`, and stop for Business Analyst review of
both grouping and REQs without committing or opening a pull request. Every REQ
must retain full evidence provenance and reference exactly one valid same-intake
group; grouping never replaces provenance or permits bundled requirements.

After presenting the completed validation and review summary, ask exactly one
question: whether the Business Analyst wants to submit the reviewed
requirements now. Do not ask before the review summary, and do not treat the
original prepare invocation as submission consent. If the answer is no, absent,
or unclear, stop with the files uncommitted. If the answer is explicitly yes,
continue into Submit mode.

## Submit mode

Use this mode when the invocation contains `--submit` or when the Business
Analyst explicitly accepts the post-review submission prompt. Treat either
action as confirmation that the Business Analyst completed the local
requirement review; it does not approve the human Requirement gate.

Resolve exactly one accepted `INTK-####` linked to the supplied issue. Do not
regenerate requirement content or modify authored files. Require every
intake-scoped REQ to have status `reviewed`, require the group registry and
every assignment to have completed human Requirement review, require all
recorded clarification questions to be closed with a named human decider and
ISO date, regenerate the requirements index, run
`python scripts/compile_requirements.py --check`, and run
`python scripts/validate_reqs.py`. Stop if any REQ is not reviewed, any group is
empty/orphaned, any assignment is missing/invalid, any question remains open,
provenance is invalid, the index is stale, or validation fails.

Create a focused branch and stage only `intake/_index.md`,
`specs/intakes/INTK-####/requirement-groups.yml`,
`specs/intakes/INTK-####/requirements.md`, and the authoritative REQ files under
`specs/intakes/INTK-####/requirements/`. Never stage raw intake documents,
`audit/`, temporary files, or unrelated changes. Check the staged diff before
committing. Commit, push, and open one pull request with the configured
Requirement title. Its body must contain `Closes #<issue-number>`, the
`INTK-####`, the REQ range and count, validation results, a clarification
closure summary, the reviewed group IDs/counts, and an unchecked human
Requirement-review checklist. If an
open pull request already exists for the same issue and intake, report it
instead of creating a duplicate. Stop before approval or merge.
